solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Record speed, about one minute — notice difference

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record

indicators.note: about means going around, so the speed word is wrapped around the one-and-minute letters

parts.note: rate is speed, as in a rate of knots
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone clocking a record's playing speed and a stopwatch reading spots that something has changed.
explanation.definitionFit: To discriminate is to perceive or note a distinction between things, a synonym for noticing a difference.

clue.text: Garibaldi, say, secure at island after revolution

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so the secure-at-island letters are read backwards

parts.note: to nail something is to fasten or secure it

explanation.surface: The Italian revolutionary Garibaldi seizes an island in the wake of an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Garibaldi, hero of Italian unification, is an example of a native of Italy; 'say' flags the example.

clue.text: Liqueur cheered Met men after storm

indicators.note: a storm throws things into disorder, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Police officers who were cheered after a storm celebrate with a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Crème de menthe is a sweet mint-flavoured liqueur, an example of the general term.

clue.text: Provoke using popular quote

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
to cite is to quote a source

explanation.surface: Stirring up trouble by quoting something popular.
explanation.definitionFit: To incite is to stir up or urge on, a synonym for provoking a reaction.

clue.text: Breaking promise over country crime?

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the first part above the second
breaking something smashes it into pieces, so the letters of the vow word are rearranged

parts.note: a nation is a country

explanation.surface: A broken promise affecting a whole country might count as a national crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Impersonating someone, such as a police officer, can be an offence; the question mark admits it is only sometimes criminal.

clue.text: Expect to be away briefly at computer study

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: taken as written before the cut
IT, information technology, is the study of computers

explanation.surface: Someone expects to be away from home for a short spell of computer training.
explanation.definitionFit: To await something is to wait for it, to anticipate or expect its arrival.

clue.text: Ultimately horrible indeed — mineral that's not nice to see

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of horrible is used

parts.note: yes, indeed, used as an affirmation
ore is mineral-bearing rock

explanation.surface: A horrible mineral specimen that is unpleasant to look at.
explanation.definitionFit: An ugly sight that offends the viewer is the idiomatic sense: something unpleasant to look at.

clue.text: Tip: horse is not trying, just starting

indicators.note: only the starting letter of each of the four words is used

explanation.surface: A racing tip: the horse isn't trying, so don't back it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tip is a piece of advice or a clue, a synonym for a suggestion.

clue.text: Picture firm haggle regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter is taken

explanation.surface: A picture's price is something to haggle over firmly.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a picture or likeness of something, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Successful period in Cricket Club, Laker's content to get party food?

indicators.note: in places the successful-period letters between the two club letters

parts.note: an up is a good spell, as in ups and downs

indicators.note: content means what is inside, so the middle letters of the name are taken

explanation.surface: During a good spell at the cricket club, the spinner Jim Laker happily tucks into the party food.
explanation.walkthrough: Jim Laker was a famous English off-spin bowler; his name's inner letters give AKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Small iced cakes are an example of food served at children's parties, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Missile shelter Rhode Island Democrat enters

indicators.note: enters says these letters go inside the shelter word

parts.note: a tent is a shelter
RI is the postal abbreviation for the US state
D is the abbreviation for a US Democrat

explanation.surface: An American politician takes cover in a missile shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: Trident is the submarine-launched nuclear missile system used by the US and UK navies.

clue.text: Garret room to some extent reminiscent of past

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An attic room that has an old-fashioned feel to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Retro describes styles that imitate or evoke an earlier era, so it recalls the past.

clue.text: Transport prisoner, extremely volatile at end of day

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so the first and last letters are taken
only the final letter of day is used

explanation.surface: A volatile prisoner is moved at the end of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: To convey is to carry or transport something from one place to another.

clue.text: Mechanic has sister holding frame

indicators.note: the phrase holds the letters within it, running across the word breaks

explanation.surface: A mechanic's sister is holding up the frame of a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A chassis is the base frame of a motor vehicle on which the body is mounted.

clue.text: Strongly dislike oath dividing the French

indicators.note: dividing means splitting apart, so the oath letters sit between the two letters of the French article

parts.note: le is French for the
taken as written

explanation.surface: An oath that splits the French, perhaps one they hate.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe is to detest or hate, a strong form of disliking.

clue.text: Not like novel writer

indicators.note: novel means new or fresh, so the two words are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Unlike a writer of novels, or perhaps not the novel a writer likes.
explanation.definitionFit: J. R. R. Tolkien, author of The Lord of the Rings, is an example of a writer.

clue.text: A wanderer having left for year? Heavenly?

indicators.note: having left for year says the left letter replaces the year letter

parts.note: a stray is an animal that wanders without a home

explanation.surface: A wanderer who has left for a year has perhaps gone to heaven.
explanation.definitionFit: Astral means relating to the stars, so of the heavens.

clue.text: Strange plea associated with introduction of passion fruit

indicators.note: strange means odd or out of order, so these letters are rearranged
the introduction is the opening, so just the first letter of passion is used

explanation.surface: An odd plea for passion fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passion fruit' looks like one item, but 'passion' supplies only P and 'fruit' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An apple is a common example of a fruit.

clue.text: Quiet nobleman one valued

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet
an earl is a nobleman

explanation.surface: A quiet aristocrat who is held in high esteem.
explanation.definitionFit: A highly prized person or thing is idiomatically a gem, as in a jewel of great price.

clue.text: Concession about name for shellfish

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the concession letters go around the name word

parts.note: a sop is a small concession made to placate someone
to call someone something is to name them

explanation.surface: A concession made over what to call a seafood dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Scallops are bivalve molluscs, an example of shellfish.

clue.text: Opening centre with parking for 100

indicators.note: parking for 100 says the parking letter takes the place of the numeral

parts.note: the core is the centre of something
C is the Roman numeral for 100
P is the standard sign for parking

explanation.surface: A central car park opens with room for a hundred vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: A pore is a tiny opening in the skin or a leaf, so a small aperture.

clue.text: Society to be important? Just a small amount

parts.note: to matter is to be important

explanation.surface: Does society matter? Only a little.
explanation.definitionFit: A smatter, like a smattering, is a slight or superficial amount, especially of knowledge.

clue.text: Comparatively risky to ignore daughter becoming more aloof

indicators.note: to ignore something is to leave it out, so the daughter letter is dropped

parts.note: dicier is the comparative of dicey, risky

explanation.surface: Neglecting a daughter is risky and makes a parent ever more distant.
explanation.definitionFit: Icy describes a cold, unfriendly manner, so the comparative means colder and more distant.

clue.text: Residual hope of award for second learner — in repeatedly, good

parts.note: a silver medal is the award for coming second
L is the learner-driver plate

indicators.note: repeatedly says the word in is written twice

explanation.surface: A learner keeps getting a silver medal, which gives them hope.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'every cloud has a silver lining' names the consoling good aspect remaining in bad news, so remaining hope.
